title: Removing stitches
subtitle: How to unpick needlework without damaging the cloth or the surrounding work.
excerpt: Removing stitches from needlework requires patience and a seam ripper or pointed scissors rather than brute force. The goal is to cut each stitch individually without pulling threads that run through the same holes as your neighbours.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Correction and repair in needlework.
Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746. Unpicking and correction methods.

glossaryTerms.definition: Needlework slang for removing stitches, from the sound 'rip it, rip it'. Any level of unpicking from a single stitch to an entire section.

content.text: , is a normal part of needlework. The goal is to remove the thread without pulling or distorting the cloth, and without cutting the neighbouring stitches that share the same holes.
Work in good light and under magnification if needed. Identify exactly which stitches are to be removed.
Starting at the last stitch worked, slip the point of the embroidery scissors under one arm of the stitch on the back of the cloth. Cut that single thread.
Use the blunt end of the needle or tweezers to gently pull the cut ends free. Do not pull hard; ease the thread out of the cloth gently.
Work backward one stitch at a time. Do not try to pull a long run of thread out in one movement: the thread passes through the same holes as neighbouring stitches and will carry them with it.

Once the stitches are removed, smooth the cloth gently with your fingers and check the holes are not permanently distorted. On Aida, the holes spring back; on linen, gently ease the weave back into position with a needle.

attrs.heading: What goes wrong
attrs.intro: Unpicking problems and how to prevent them.

items.symptom: Neighbouring stitches unravel with the ones being removed
items.cause: The thread was pulled rather than cut individually.
items.fix: Cut each stitch individually. Pull out only one cut stitch at a time.

items.symptom: A hole or permanent distortion remains in the cloth
items.cause: The thread was pulled hard through the cloth.
items.fix: Gentle is essential. If a hole remains, wash the cloth and press while slightly damp to help the weave close.

content.text: Careful unpicking is a skill every stitcher needs. Even experienced needleworkers remove sections at times. Doing it cleanly stops the cloth from getting fuzzy.
